correctness.rationale: From the exact fourth-order apex survival probability, swift evolution is equivalent to B1=0 after unitary apex gauge fixing; its excess coefficient is ||B1||²/12. Degree-two subdivision rows give opposite endpoint phases, and degree-three rows require triples of equilateral unit phases. A path in the original graph alternates local cube-root cosets, so odd cycles are impossible. For bipartite cubic G, Hall plus 2-factor cycle alternation yields a proper 3-edge-colouring, and the explicit phases cancel on each row. Connectivity and the free global action of cube roots give the complete phase parametrization. The invariant 2D subspace proves the all-time probability law and uniform terminal probabilities. This verifies all finite simple connected cubic graphs with unit-modulus, zero diagonal bonds and no unproved extrapolation. The actual embedded Python checker replays exact cancellations and fourth moments plus independent finite Taylor computations.

Its full accessible text and relevant appendix were inspected; the new parity necessity, sufficiency construction and circle-count formula are not stated. The paper may supply the preliminary lemma but not the claimed implication. Literature and published-findings index searches found no equivalent result. value.rationale: This is an exact phase-only quantum-transport design classification for a natural nonregular network family generated by subdividing physical couplings. It determines whether the quantum speed limit and equal-probability arrival can both be attained, gives explicit phase controls via a classical edge-colouring, and identifies a parity obstruction invisible to original 3-edge-colourability (e.g. K4 versus K3,3). The complete family and solution-manifold count are substantive invariants rather than an arbitrary finite slice or textbook restatement.
